facts.text: run-to-goal-ants-v0 is registered with entry point gym_compete.new_envs:MultiAgentEnv, two ant agents, the ant scene XML and the initial positions [(-1, 0, 0.75), (1, 0, 0.75)]
MultiAgentEnv builds observation_space and action_space as a Tuple with one entry per agent
MultiAgentEnv._step advances the scene, collects per-agent rewards, dones and infos, and returns a tuple of per-agent observations
MultiAgentScene.simulate concatenates the per-agent actions and calls do_simulation with the scene's frame_skip
MultiAgentScene constructs gym's MuJoCo environment with frame_skip 5
The ant scene XML sets the MuJoCo timestep to 0.01 s
Agent.set_action_space builds each agent's Box from the XML actuator ctrlrange and falls back to infinite bounds when no range is found
The ant XML declares eight motors with ctrlrange -1.0 to 1.0
The ant observation concatenates its qpos, qvel, clipped external contact forces and the other agent's qpos
The ant observation space is Box(-inf, inf) with the observation size computed from that observation
MultiAgentEnv._seed delegates seeding to the scene
MultiAgentEnv.reset_model resets the scene and every agent and returns the per-agent observations
The tested stack is gym 0.9.1 with MuJoCo 1.31 and mujoco-py 0.5.7 on Python 3.6

determinism.notes: seed() or reset(seed) fixes the fake's initial joint offsets and the kinematic update is deterministic, so one seed and one action sequence repeat a state-hash trajectory; the upstream MuJoCo scene uses gym's and MuJoCo's generators, and this fake uses Python's random.Random, so a seed does not give the same trajectory on the two

fidelity.engine: gym-compete:run-to-goal-ants-v0 (legacy gym 0.9.1 + MuJoCo 1.31 on the sim backend; the fake backend is an analytic kinematic stand-in)
gaps: the fake backend is kinematic: no MuJoCo rigid-body integration, contact solver, actuator, sensor or noise model is implemented, and its external contact forces are reported as zero

one environment step is 50 ms: the MuJoCo timestep in the ant scene XML is 0.01 s (world XML:4) and MultiAgentScene passes frame_skip 5 (multi_agent_scene.py:12), so the contract exposes the 50 ms control-step period as timestep_ms and one step contains five 10 ms integrations

the upstream MultiAgentEnv returns a tuple of per-agent rewards and a tuple of per-agent dones; cap.world.step.v1 carries one scalar reward and one scalar terminal flag, so the fake sums the rewards, terminates when any agent is done and keeps the per-agent values in info
the upstream legacy gym reset returns a bare observation tuple; the bridge reads a reset two-tuple as (observation, info), so the fake returns (observations, {})
no wall-clock pacing: realtime_factor 0, ticks advance simulated time only
the fake has no goal, fall, arena or rendering logic, no per-agent policies and no demo policies; it was never compared with the upstream MuJoCo environment
the sim backend (gym.make of the legacy environment) needs gym 0.9.1, mujoco-py 0.5.7 and MuJoCo 1.31 and was not run

measures.description: Last observation (derived from the observation space)
measures.name: observation

safe_state.description: the simulation stops advancing: no step or reset is accepted after an e-stop until mhs.safety.reset clears the latch; the environment state is kept and stays readable
